groups.canonical_citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.63
groups.conflict_note: Official ordinance text does not state a separate effective date beyond Council passage (Nov 18, 2025); a secondary source estimates an effective date of January 2026.
groups.interaction: Overlaps with the CA Cartwright Act (Bus. & Prof. Code §16729) banning algorithmic pricing collusion statewide; the local ordinance adds city-specific civil penalties and a private right of action.

groups.canonical_citation: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.106
groups.interaction: State law (Gov. Code §12955/Civil Rights Council regs) restricts but does not entirely bar use of criminal history; Berkeley's ordinance imposes a stricter, near-total local ban.

groups.canonical_citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76 (Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB)
groups.conflict_note: Sources give different effective dates for different components (e.g., relocation payment increases effective 2026-01-01; Measure BB passed the Nov 2024 election without one stated effective date for the nonpayment threshold change).
groups.interaction: Because this is a local just-cause ordinance adopted before Sept 1, 2019, it displaces the default state just-cause requirement under Civ. Code §1946.2 for covered Berkeley units.
Works alongside the state screening-fee cap under Civ. Code §1950.6; requires disclosure of the state cap and adds a separate local prohibition on non-refundable renewal/roommate fees.

groups.canonical_citation: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.76.110A (Rent Stabilization Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB)
groups.conflict_note: Measure BB (Nov 2024) capped the Annual General Adjustment formula at 5%; the 2026 Rent Board order sets the actual AGA at 1.0%, both under the same ch. 13.76 regime.
groups.interaction: The state AB 1482 rent cap does not apply to units covered by Berkeley's local rent control ordinance, which imposes its own stricter annual cap.

groups.canonical_citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance - Security Deposit Interest)
groups.interaction: Supplements the state deposit cap (Civ. Code §1950.5) by requiring interest payments on deposits for rent-controlled units.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6
groups.conflict_note: Base cap is $30 (1998), CPI-adjusted annually; the 2026 cap is $68.96.
groups.interaction: Applies statewide; local ordinances such as Berkeley's require disclosure of this cap but cannot set a different cap amount.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (FEHA, as amended by SB 329)
groups.conflict_note: SB 329 (effective 2020-01-01) established source-of-income protections; a later amendment described in one source (effective 2024-01-01) added a requirement to accept alternative income proof for subsidized tenants; sources cite different effective dates for different amendments to the same code section.
groups.interaction: Applies statewide to all landlords regardless of local ordinances; no local override identified.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 2 (Civil Rights Council Criminal History Regulations); Cal. Gov. Code § 12955
groups.conflict_note: One source lacks a specific statutory/regulatory citation and infers authority from general FEHA; exact regulatory citation is uncertain across sources.
groups.interaction: Berkeley's Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance imposes a stricter, near-total ban on criminal history inquiries beyond this state regulation's limits.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (as amended by SB 267)
groups.conflict_note: Effective date not stated in source; SB 267 was enacted in 2023, presumed effective 2024-01-01.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729
groups.conflict_note: No explicit effective date in statutory text; California bills without urgency clauses typically take effect Jan 1 following enactment, consistent with a secondary source's stated 2026-01-01 date.
groups.interaction: Operates alongside (not preempting) local algorithmic rent-setting bans in Berkeley, San Diego, and Santa Ana, which add housing-specific penalties and private rights of action.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 (Tenant Protection Act of 2019, as amended)
groups.conflict_note: Underlying section originally effective 2020-01-01; the version addressing interaction with local ordinances became operative 2024-04-01; a later amendment is effective 2026-01-01; the section is set to self-repeal 2030-01-01.
groups.interaction: Does not apply where a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before Sept 1, 2019 (or a more protective later one) governs instead, e.g., in Berkeley, San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, and Santa Ana.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 (Tenant Protection Act of 2019 / AB 1482)
groups.conflict_note: Operative date differs from original enactment (Jan 1, 2020); section is repealed as of Jan 1, 2030.
groups.interaction: Does not apply to units covered by a more protective local rent control ordinance, such as those in Berkeley, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Santa Ana.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5
groups.conflict_note: Deposit-amount cap effective 2024-07-01 (AB 12); separate itemization/nonrefundable provisions amended by AB 414 effective 2026-01-01.
groups.interaction: Local ordinances (e.g., Berkeley) may add additional requirements such as interest payment on deposits, supplementing but not conflicting with this state cap.

groups.canonical_citation: L.A.M.C. §§151.09, 165.03, 165.05, 165.06 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance & Just Cause Ordinance)
groups.conflict_note: Relocation assistance amounts vary annually (current figures for 7/1/2026-6/30/2027) and overlap with state Housing Crisis Act requirements, which may require higher payments for lower-income tenants displaced for new construction (Resident Protections Ordinance, effective 2025-02-11).
groups.interaction: As a local just-cause ordinance adopted before Sept 1, 2019, this ordinance displaces the state Tenant Protection Act default; where state Housing Crisis Act relocation requirements exceed local RSO/JCO amounts, landlords must pay the higher amount.

groups.canonical_citation: L.A.M.C. § 151.06 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance)
groups.conflict_note: Annual allowable percentage changes each year (3% for 7/1/2025-6/30/2026); separate surcharge pass-throughs (RSO/SCEP fees) have different effective dates (2020, 2022).
groups.interaction: The state AB 1482 rent cap does not apply to units covered by this local RSO, which has its own stricter annual cap and separate fee surcharges.
Supplements state FEHA source-of-income protections with city-specific anti-discrimination enforcement provisions.
Adds an interest-payment requirement for rent-stabilized units beyond the state deposit cap under Civ. Code §1950.5.

groups.canonical_citation: San Diego Mun. Code §§98.0700-98.0707 (Residential Tenant Protection Ordinance)
groups.conflict_note: Section 98.0706 was amended 2024-02-27 (effective 2024-03-28); the original ordinance was effective 2023-06-24.
groups.interaction: Operates alongside and consistent with the state Tenant Protection Act (Civ. Code §1946.2), adding local relocation assistance and buyout protections; as a local just-cause ordinance it displaces the default state rule for covered units.

groups.canonical_citation: San Diego Mun. Code § 98.1103
groups.conflict_note: A draft staff report left the final passage date blank, suggesting the ordinance may still have been pending at drafting, but the same code section confirms enactment; treated as enacted since an official code citation exists.
groups.interaction: Operates alongside the state Cartwright Act's ban on common pricing algorithms, adding city-specific penalties and a private right of action.

groups.conflict_note: Relocation payment amounts adjust annually (current figures for 3/1/2026-2/28/2027).
groups.interaction: As a local just-cause ordinance adopted before Sept 1, 2019, this ordinance displaces the state Tenant Protection Act default for covered units.

groups.canonical_citation: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.3
groups.conflict_note: Rate is set annually; units built after June 13, 1979 or governed by Costa-Hawkins are exempt from this cap though still subject to just-cause protections.
groups.interaction: The state AB 1482 rent cap does not apply to units covered by this local rent control ordinance.

groups.canonical_citation: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C
groups.interaction: Operates alongside the state Cartwright Act amendment banning common pricing algorithms statewide.

groups.canonical_citation: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A(e)
groups.interaction: Supplements the state deposit cap (Civ. Code §1950.5) by requiring annual interest payment on deposits at a locally-set rate.

groups.canonical_citation: Santa Ana Mun. Code, Rent Stabilization Ordinance
groups.conflict_note: Current allowable increase percentage adjusts annually (2.87% for 9/1/2026-8/31/2027).
groups.interaction: The state AB 1482 rent cap does not apply to units covered by this local rent control ordinance.

groups.canonical_citation: Santa Ana Mun. Code, Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
groups.interaction: As a local just-cause ordinance adopted before Sept 1, 2019, this ordinance displaces the state Tenant Protection Act default for covered units.

groups.canonical_citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (Registration Fee Pass-Through Cap)
Santa Ana Ordinance (Algorithmic Rent-Setting Software Ban)
groups.conflict_note: One source describes the ordinance as pending a final vote scheduled March 3, 2026 (after first reading Feb 17, 2026); another describes it as already enacted/in effect; treated as enacted per final adoption, with uncertainty about the exact effective date.
groups.interaction: Operates alongside the state Cartwright Act's ban on common pricing algorithms, adding city-specific penalties.
